page.layout: Running head at top centre: "EPISTOLA." One text column: first a continuation of a letter (6 lines), then two right-aligned closing lines (signature and "&c."), then a decorative rule, then the heading "ERRATA." and a errata paragraph in one column, full width. No margin notes, no page number, no catchword.

main_text.l: bus apud Deum contendit pro nobis nostrarumque
Ecclesiarum pace ac salute, quem & nos obnixe o-
ramus, ut Ecclesias vestras æternum incolumes &
florentes esse velit, vobisque & vestris laboribus ita
propicius sit, ut mortalitatis hoc stadio feliciter in
munere decurso, pa[?]nam cœlestem assequamini.
V.R.W. Addictiss. &c.
A.R. & cæt.
ERRATA.
CUm typothetæ familiariter satis cognita
noit[?] fuerit Authoris manus ; fieri non potuit quin
complura subrepserint errata ; nam præter ea
quæ in distinctionum notis sunt, occurrent frequen-
tia satis in literis : ita quidem ut sæpius sit numeri
singularis pro plurali & vice versa permutatio, quæ
humanus Lector condonabit, & facile per se corri-
get. Ante lectionem vero monendus es ut hæc pau-
cula sic emendes, pag. 193. lin. 6. post ad sess. adde
16. pag. 259. & pag. 197. lin. 2. post ad sess. adde. 16.
pag. 241. Et pag. 266. 15. pro quæstus fuit male, le-
gendum, monuit sibi videri non satis commode. & eadem
pag. lin. 24. post quæstionis, adde, cujus sententia

l.i: fuit removendos & abjurandos, licet vix sibi persuaderet

page.notes: The word after "pa" in the first paragraph is partly covered by a mark and show-through; read as "pa[?]nam". "noit" in the errata paragraph is doubtful (rendered as "noii"). A handwritten number at the foot of the page ("401 /4 76 089") is not printed and is left out. Stains and ornaments in the left margin and around the rule are not text.
